world.title: Ukraine denies report Trump urged Zelensky to meet Putin
world.summary: Ukraine’s President’s Office denied a Bloomberg report that President Donald Trump urged President Volodymyr Zelensky to travel to Moscow for talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin, calling it false. Bloomberg, citing people familiar with the conversation, reported that Zelensky rejected the suggestion and was ups
world.content: Ukraine’s President’s Office denied a Bloomberg report that President Donald Trump urged President Volodymyr Zelensky to travel to Moscow for talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin, calling it false. Bloomberg, citing people familiar with the conversation, reported that Zelensky rejected the suggestion and was upset by it. The White House did not respond to Bloomberg’s request for comment. Separately, Zelensky said he asked Trump to press Chinese President Xi Jinping to use Beijing’s influence with Moscow to help end Russia’s invasion. Zelensky said Washington was proposing technical-level talks among U.S., Ukrainian and Russian delegations without the countries’ leaders. He said the talks were likely to take place in the United Arab Emirates, while Ukraine awaited a date from Washington.
world.image_alt: Ukraine denies report Trump urged Zelensky to meet Putin

world.title: Yemen
world.summary: Yemen’s internationally recognized leader, Rashad al-Alimi, called on Yemenis to join government armed and security forces in a televised address Friday, Sept. 25. He said the campaign would restore state institutions and extend government sovereignty across the country, including to the Houthi-held capital, Sanaa. Al-
world.content: Yemen’s internationally recognized leader, Rashad al-Alimi, called on Yemenis to join government armed and security forces in a televised address Friday, Sept. 25. He said the campaign would restore state institutions and extend government sovereignty across the country, including to the Houthi-held capital, Sanaa. Al-Alimi also offered a general amnesty to Houthi fighters and affiliates who leave the movement and stop fighting or working for it, subject to legal procedures. The appeal followed a sharp escalation in fighting, including Houthi advances along Yemen’s Red Sea coast and attacks on Saudi Arabia. The Houthis have also imposed a naval blockade on Saudi vessels.

world.title: Saudi coalition intercepts Houthi drones, missiles aimed at kingdom
world.summary: Saudi Arabia’s coalition in Yemen said on Saturday, Sept. 26, that air defenses intercepted two drones launched toward the Riyadh region and two ballistic missiles aimed at Khamis Mushait in the kingdom’s southwest. Coalition spokesman Turki Al-Maliki said forces were monitoring missile and drone threats. The coalition
world.content: Saudi Arabia’s coalition in Yemen said on Saturday, Sept. 26, that air defenses intercepted two drones launched toward the Riyadh region and two ballistic missiles aimed at Khamis Mushait in the kingdom’s southwest. Coalition spokesman Turki Al-Maliki said forces were monitoring missile and drone threats. The coalition provided no further operational details. The Houthis have attacked Saudi cities and shipping since declaring a naval blockade against the kingdom in July.
world.image_alt: Saudi coalition intercepts Houthi drones, missiles aimed at kingdom

world.title: Putin keeps peace proposals open, denies plans to attack Europe
world.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin said on Sept. 25 that proposals to resume peace talks with Ukraine remained available, but Moscow would decide whether to negotiate based on Russia’s interests. He linked the decision to what he described as recent Ukrainian attacks on Russian territory and said Russia would consider it
world.content: Russian President Vladimir Putin said on Sept. 25 that proposals to resume peace talks with Ukraine remained available, but Moscow would decide whether to negotiate based on Russia’s interests. He linked the decision to what he described as recent Ukrainian attacks on Russian territory and said Russia would consider its response before taking further steps. At a news conference in St. Petersburg, Putin said Russia was not preparing for military action against Europe and accused European countries of raising tensions by supporting Ukraine. His comments followed warnings from European NATO members of possible Russian threats. The articles reported both those warnings and Putin’s account of the attacks as competing claims that were not independently established.
world.image_alt: Putin keeps peace proposals open, denies plans to attack Europe

world.title: UN adds 61 firms to West Bank settlements database
world.summary: The U.N. human rights office added 61 companies to its database of businesses linked to Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank, bringing the total to 214 firms in 11 countries; most are Israeli. Five companies on the previous list were removed. The additions include Israeli pesticide maker ADAMA, real estate com
world.content: The U.N. human rights office added 61 companies to its database of businesses linked to Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank, bringing the total to 214 firms in 11 countries; most are Israeli. Five companies on the previous list were removed. The additions include Israeli pesticide maker ADAMA, real estate company Alony Hetz and Spain-based Salvat Logistica. The U.N. said the database identifies businesses involved in settlement-related activities and that companies are expected to meet their human rights responsibilities. Israel’s diplomatic mission denounced the database as a distorted mechanism that unfairly targets the country.
world.image_alt: UN adds 61 firms to West Bank settlements database

world.title: Ethiopia’s Tigray rebels seize airports as fighting spreads
world.summary: Fighting between Ethiopia’s federal forces and Tigrayan forces intensified this week in the northern Tigray region and spread into neighboring Afar and Amhara. The Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF) said it was again in "full-blown war" with the government after taking control of local airports. Federal officials
world.content: Fighting between Ethiopia’s federal forces and Tigrayan forces intensified this week in the northern Tigray region and spread into neighboring Afar and Amhara. The Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF) said it was again in "full-blown war" with the government after taking control of local airports. Federal officials and Tigrayan leaders blamed each other for starting the latest escalation. The TPLF has joined six other armed groups in an alliance seeking to remove Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed’s government. The renewed clashes follow more than six months of worsening relations and threaten the peace agreement that ended the 2020-22 war. The UN human rights chief said airstrikes, some involving drones, hit five schools in Tigray on Sept. 22, causing deaths and injuries. He also said a mortar strike in Kobo on Sept. 23 reportedly killed civilians. Phone and internet services have been disrupted in the north.
world.image_alt: Ethiopia’s Tigray rebels seize airports as fighting spreads

world.title: Brazil
world.summary: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva signed a provisional measure on Sept. 25 banning online fixed-odds betting and casino operations, including their promotion and intermediation. It took effect immediately: users could no longer add funds but had until 11:59 p.m. on Oct. 5 to withdraw balances; betting platf
world.content: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva signed a provisional measure on Sept. 25 banning online fixed-odds betting and casino operations, including their promotion and intermediation. It took effect immediately: users could no longer add funds but had until 11:59 p.m. on Oct. 5 to withdraw balances; betting platforms were due to stop operating on Oct. 6. Congress must approve the measure within 120 days for it to remain in force. Lula’s government said the ban addresses gambling addiction, household debt and the transfer of family funds to betting companies. The announcement came nine days before the Oct. 4 first round of the presidential election, with polls showing Lula in a close race with right-wing senator Flávio Bolsonaro.

world.title: Bangkok declares disaster across 50 districts after flooding
world.summary: Bangkok authorities declared a disaster across all 50 districts on Saturday, Sept. 26, after nearly 300 millimeters (11.8 inches) of rain had fallen in the Thai capital since Thursday afternoon. The designation allows local organizations to take emergency action. Flooding submerged roads, filled canals and inundated ho
world.content: Bangkok authorities declared a disaster across all 50 districts on Saturday, Sept. 26, after nearly 300 millimeters (11.8 inches) of rain had fallen in the Thai capital since Thursday afternoon. The designation allows local organizations to take emergency action. Flooding submerged roads, filled canals and inundated homes and restaurants, with eastern Bangkok among the hardest-hit areas. At least two people died, and flooding has affected more than 84,000 people in 21 provinces nationwide. Thailand’s Meteorological Department warned that heavy rain would continue across much of the country through Sunday, Sept. 27.
world.image_alt: Bangkok declares disaster across 50 districts after flooding

business.summary: A working paper by economists Robert Fairlie and Jane Wu examines hiring of recent college graduates, based on the premise that labor-demand changes may first appear in reduced hiring as AI takes on standardized tasks common in entry-level office jobs. Graduates also face a hiring process increasingly shaped by AI tool
business.content: A working paper by economists Robert Fairlie and Jane Wu examines hiring of recent college graduates, based on the premise that labor-demand changes may first appear in reduced hiring as AI takes on standardized tasks common in entry-level office jobs. Graduates also face a hiring process increasingly shaped by AI tools and employer demand for AI skills.

business.title: Beckham takes £38.5m as World Cup deals lift profits
business.summary: David Beckham’s brand and commercial group, DRJB Holdings, reported record 2025 revenue of £84 million, up 20% from £72.2 million, and pre-tax profit of about £50 million, a 46% increase. Advertising partnerships signed ahead of the 2026 World Cup helped drive results; Beckham appeared in campaigns for brands including
business.content: David Beckham’s brand and commercial group, DRJB Holdings, reported record 2025 revenue of £84 million, up 20% from £72.2 million, and pre-tax profit of about £50 million, a 46% increase. Advertising partnerships signed ahead of the 2026 World Cup helped drive results; Beckham appeared in campaigns for brands including Bank of America, McDonald’s, Verizon and PepsiCo’s Lay’s. DRJB paid shareholders £38.9 million in dividends for the year and made a further £46.6 million payment after the financial year ended. Beckham owns 45% of the group, with Authentic Brands Group holding the remaining 55%; his share of the two distributions was estimated at about £38.5 million.
business.image_alt: Beckham takes £38.5m as World Cup deals lift profits

business.title: Bill Gates urges mandatory AI safeguards after billion-death warning
business.summary: Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates said in an NBC “Meet the Press” interview excerpt that AI could drive events causing a billion deaths if people with malicious intent use advanced tools. He framed the figure as a possible catastrophic outcome, not a prediction, and said industry self-regulation would not be sufficient.
business.content: Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates said in an NBC “Meet the Press” interview excerpt that AI could drive events causing a billion deaths if people with malicious intent use advanced tools. He framed the figure as a possible catastrophic outcome, not a prediction, and said industry self-regulation would not be sufficient. Gates called for stronger AI oversight. Leading developers have also called for stronger guardrails after security incidents, while Trump has downplayed AI risks and encouraged AI development.
business.image_alt: Bill Gates urges mandatory AI safeguards after billion-death warning

business.title: U.S. appeals court upholds Pentagon
business.summary: A three-judge panel of the U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit ruled 2-1 on Sept. 25 that the Pentagon could designate Anthropic a national-security supply-chain risk under a 2018 federal procurement law. The decision lets the Defense Department exclude Anthropic’s Claude models from its systems and bar contract
business.content: A three-judge panel of the U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit ruled 2-1 on Sept. 25 that the Pentagon could designate Anthropic a national-security supply-chain risk under a 2018 federal procurement law. The decision lets the Defense Department exclude Anthropic’s Claude models from its systems and bar contractors from using them on Defense Department work. The dispute followed Anthropic’s refusal to remove restrictions against using its models for lethal autonomous weapons and domestic mass surveillance. The majority said the restrictions could prevent Claude from carrying out military tasks the department considers authorized and necessary. Anthropic says the designation has cost it billions of dollars in potential business and damaged its reputation ahead of a planned initial public offering. The ruling concerns a separate legal basis from an August federal court decision in California that blocked a broader government restriction under another legal authority; Anthropic said it was considering further review.

business.summary: Farmers in the United States and England are facing financial pressure from higher production costs, poor harvests and limited public support. business.content: Farmers in the United States and England are facing financial pressure from higher production costs, poor harvests and limited public support. U.S. growers face another year of losses as soaring fuel and fertilizer costs offset higher revenue, NPR reported Sept. 25. Rick Telesz, who farms about 700 acres in Pennsylvania, said he may only break even on corn and soybeans. In England, the 2026 Sustainable Farming Incentive ran out of funding six hours after applications opened Tuesday, Sept. 22, leaving some farmers unable to secure payments after repeated website errors. The Guardian reported that applicants sought funding for environmental practices after successive poor harvests.

business.title: U.S. seeks to join Musk
business.summary: The U.S. Justice Department has asked the European Union’s General Court to let the United States intervene in Elon Musk and X’s challenge to a €120 million fine imposed by the European Commission in December 2025. The penalty was the first issued under the EU’s Digital Services Act (DSA), and the Commission said X vio
business.content: The U.S. Justice Department has asked the European Union’s General Court to let the United States intervene in Elon Musk and X’s challenge to a €120 million fine imposed by the European Commission in December 2025. The penalty was the first issued under the EU’s Digital Services Act (DSA), and the Commission said X violated rules involving its blue-check verification system, advertising transparency and researchers’ access to public data. The Justice Department argues that the Commission improperly extended its authority over U.S. companies. The General Court will decide whether to allow the U.S. to intervene.

business.title: Volkswagen recalls 2.86 million vehicles over steering risk
business.summary: Volkswagen Group is recalling about 2.86 million Volkswagen and Audi vehicles worldwide after quality checks identified a steering-system fastener that could corrode and break, potentially impairing steering control. The affected Volkswagen models are the Golf, Golf Variant, Tiguan, Touran and Caddy, built from Sept. 2
business.content: Volkswagen Group is recalling about 2.86 million Volkswagen and Audi vehicles worldwide after quality checks identified a steering-system fastener that could corrode and break, potentially impairing steering control. The affected Volkswagen models are the Golf, Golf Variant, Tiguan, Touran and Caddy, built from Sept. 24, 2013, to July 1, 2024. Audi Q3s built from Oct. 31, 2017, to May 23, 2024, are also included. Germany's Federal Motor Transport Authority said a broken bolt could cause steering failure. The campaign covers 2,159,054 Volkswagen vehicles and 696,547 Audis, including about 954,000 vehicles in Germany. Authorities and the companies reported no related injuries or property damage. Dealers will replace the affected fastener at no charge.
business.image_alt: Volkswagen recalls 2.86 million vehicles over steering risk

science.title: Climate overshoot can leave lasting damage after temperatures fall
science.summary: A Concordia-led study published in *Communications Earth & Environment* found that returning global temperatures to a climate target does not necessarily reverse damage caused by temporarily exceeding it. Climate overshoot occurs when temperatures rise above a target before later falling.
science.content: A Concordia-led study published in *Communications Earth & Environment* found that returning global temperatures to a climate target does not necessarily reverse damage caused by temporarily exceeding it. science.content: A study published in Nature Climate Change reports that dryland ecosystems are becoming increasingly unstable, with satellite data showing a growing “boom-and-bust” pattern in greening. KVOA reported that the findings include drylands in the American Southwest.

science.title: Papua’s remaining tropical glaciers may vanish within two years
science.summary: Only small patches of snow remain around Puncak Jaya, also known as Carstensz Pyramid, in Indonesia’s Sudirman Range, and scientists expect them to disappear within a year or two. Glacier cover around the peak has contracted from nearly 1,900 hectares in the 19th century to about 16 hectares today. The peaks have offer
science.content: Only small patches of snow remain around Puncak Jaya, also known as Carstensz Pyramid, in Indonesia’s Sudirman Range, and scientists expect them to disappear within a year or two. Glacier cover around the peak has contracted from nearly 1,900 hectares in the 19th century to about 16 hectares today. The peaks have offered scientists insights into Earth's climate history.
science.image_alt: Papua’s remaining tropical glaciers may vanish within two years

science.title: NASA and Boeing schedule Starliner development briefing Monday
science.summary: NASA and Boeing will hold a news conference at 3 p.m. EDT Monday, Sept. 28, to discuss Starliner’s development and plans for regular crew flights to and from the International Space Station. Participants will include NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman, Low Earth Orbit Program Manager Dana Weigel, astronaut Woody Hoburg
science.content: NASA and Boeing will hold a news conference at 3 p.m. EDT Monday, Sept. 28, to discuss Starliner’s development and plans for regular crew flights to and from the International Space Station. Participants will include NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman, Low Earth Orbit Program Manager Dana Weigel, astronaut Woody Hoburg and Boeing Commercial Crew Vice President John Mulholland. Starliner has not been certified for operational crew flights. The spacecraft launched NASA’s Crew Flight Test astronauts Butch Wilmore and Suni Williams and is shown docked to the station’s Harmony module.
science.image_alt: NASA and Boeing schedule Starliner development briefing Monday

science.title: Review points to 2D materials for programmable quantum photonics
science.summary: A review by TMOS researchers published in Nature Photonics examines how ultrathin materials could enable programmable quantum-photonic circuits. The review identifies new materials as a requirement for quantum-photonic technologies. The researchers identify two-dimensional materials as potential building blocks for tun
science.content: A review by TMOS researchers published in Nature Photonics examines how ultrathin materials could enable programmable quantum-photonic circuits. The review identifies new materials as a requirement for quantum-photonic technologies. The researchers identify two-dimensional materials as potential building blocks for tunable, scalable photonic circuits and describe multifunctionality as a central materials challenge.
science.image_alt: Review points to 2D materials for programmable quantum photonics

science.title: Researchers map phage genes to advance antibacterial engineering
science.summary: Researchers in New Zealand developed a method to identify genes essential to diverse bacteriophages, viruses that infect and kill bacteria. The work could give scientists a better basis for engineering phages as potential tools against harmful bacteria. Using the approach, the team identified genes that phages need to
science.content: Researchers in New Zealand developed a method to identify genes essential to diverse bacteriophages, viruses that infect and kill bacteria. The work could give scientists a better basis for engineering phages as potential tools against harmful bacteria. Using the approach, the team identified genes that phages need to survive and inserted a gene that makes the viruses fluoresce. The researchers said the method could help add other useful genes, potentially improving phages' ability to kill bacteria that harm humans.
science.image_alt: Researchers map phage genes to advance antibacterial engineering

science.title: Paleontologists report new dinosaur and bird fossil discoveries
science.summary: Paleontologists described Kayrasaurus changliensis, a feathered, plant-eating therizinosaur that lived in China’s Early Cretaceous Jehol Biota about 125 million years ago. The subadult measured more than 3.6 meters long and had large, curved claws. Separately, a fossil found in Denmark’s Early Eocene Fur Formation reve
science.content: Paleontologists described Kayrasaurus changliensis, a feathered, plant-eating therizinosaur that lived in China’s Early Cretaceous Jehol Biota about 125 million years ago. The subadult measured more than 3.6 meters long and had large, curved claws. Separately, a fossil found in Denmark’s Early Eocene Fur Formation revealed an early trogon, Daniatrogon kochi, whose second toe had not developed the permanently reversed position seen in living trogons. Other reports described feathers preserved in fossilized dinosaur droppings. Science News said the find may help address questions about plumage and survival across the end-Cretaceous asteroid impact. The Independent also reported the first series of adult Tyrannosaurus rex footprints, which researchers used to estimate the dinosaur’s walking speed. The article summary did not specify the estimate.
science.image_alt: Paleontologists report new dinosaur and bird fossil discoveries

White-ball coach Brendon McCullum devised the appointment. Pietersen said the work is part-time and that he is enjoying being back in the dressing room. Pietersen has als
sports.content: Former England batter Kevin Pietersen has returned to the national setup as a specialist mentor for the white-ball teams ahead of the 2027 World Cup. White-ball coach Brendon McCullum devised the appointment. Pietersen said the work is part-time and that he is enjoying being back in the dressing room. Pietersen has also spoken with Test coach Stephen Fleming about potentially contributing to the Test side before next summer’s Ashes, though he said the conversation does not necessarily mean he will join the dressing room.

sports.title: Arsenal forward Kai Havertz leaves Germany camp with muscle strain
sports.summary: Arsenal forward Kai Havertz is returning to his club for assessment after suffering a muscle strain during Germany’s 1-1 Nations League draw with the Netherlands in Amsterdam on Thursday. Havertz went off in the first half, around the 30-minute mark, following a collision with Netherlands midfielder Quinten Timber; the
sports.content: Arsenal forward Kai Havertz is returning to his club for assessment after suffering a muscle strain during Germany’s 1-1 Nations League draw with the Netherlands in Amsterdam on Thursday. Havertz went off in the first half, around the 30-minute mark, following a collision with Netherlands midfielder Quinten Timber; the German Football Federation confirmed the strain the next day. Germany ruled Havertz out of its next Nations League match against Greece. The federation did not provide a recovery timetable, and Arsenal’s medical staff will assess him after his return.
sports.image_alt: Arsenal forward Kai Havertz leaves Germany camp with muscle strain

sports.title: NFLPA urges field standards ahead of Cowboys-Ravens Rio game
sports.summary: NFL Players Association executive director JC Tretter raised concerns Friday, Sept. 25, about the Maracanã Stadium surface ahead of Sunday’s Dallas Cowboys-Baltimore Ravens game in Rio de Janeiro. He said loose, patchy grass could cause excessive slipping and affect players’ ability to cut and change direction. He desc
sports.content: NFL Players Association executive director JC Tretter raised concerns Friday, Sept. 25, about the Maracanã Stadium surface ahead of Sunday’s Dallas Cowboys-Baltimore Ravens game in Rio de Janeiro. He said loose, patchy grass could cause excessive slipping and affect players’ ability to cut and change direction. He described the concern primarily as one of playability and performance rather than a significant injury risk. NFL and NFLPA experts were monitoring field conditions ahead of the game.
sports.image_alt: NFLPA urges field standards ahead of Cowboys-Ravens Rio game

sports.title: Update: Fury-Joshua bout faces dispute over Dana White’s role
sports.summary: Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua are scheduled to meet on December 11 at Cardiff’s Principality Stadium, with the fight set to stream on Netflix. The bout was announced on September 24 after years of failed negotiations, but reports published two days later said a dispute over its promotion could jeopardize it. The disput
sports.content: Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua are scheduled to meet on December 11 at Cardiff’s Principality Stadium, with the fight set to stream on Netflix. The bout was announced on September 24 after years of failed negotiations, but reports published two days later said a dispute over its promotion could jeopardize it. The dispute centers on Joshua promoter Eddie Hearn’s position that Dana White is contractually barred from involvement, while the announced promotion arrangement lists Alalshikh’s The Ring and White as co-promoters. Fury said he removed a similar restriction from his own contract and supports White’s participation. The reports describe a risk of cancellation, not a confirmed cancellation.
sports.image_alt: Update: Fury-Joshua bout faces dispute over Dana White’s role

sports.title: Ireland midfielder Knight says Israel match should not be played
sports.summary: After Ireland’s 1-0 loss to Kosovo on Thursday, midfielder Jason Knight said the squad would discuss how to approach the Israel fixture. He was the first player to speak publicly about the match. The fixture is scheduled for Sunday in Debrecen, Hungary, with the return match set for October 4 in Backa Topola, Serbia. T
sports.content: After Ireland’s 1-0 loss to Kosovo on Thursday, midfielder Jason Knight said the squad would discuss how to approach the Israel fixture. He was the first player to speak publicly about the match. The fixture is scheduled for Sunday in Debrecen, Hungary, with the return match set for October 4 in Backa Topola, Serbia. The matches have prompted calls in Ireland for a boycott over Israel’s military campaign in Gaza. Ireland coach Heimir Hallgrímsson said some players felt uncomfortable about playing, and the Israel Football Association strongly criticized his remarks.
sports.image_alt: Ireland midfielder Knight says Israel match should not be played

sports.content: Warrington Wolves beat Leeds Rhinos 14-12 in a Super League play-off semi-final at Headingley on September 25 to book their first Grand Final appearance since 2018. Ewan Irwin, 18, kicked the decisive penalty after a disputed escort call against Leeds' James McDonnell. Warrington will face Wigan Warriors or Wakefield Trinity at Old Trafford on October 3. Warrington are seeking their first league title since 1955, while Leeds last won the Grand Final in 2017.
sports.image_alt: Warrington Wolves edge Leeds 14-12 to reach Grand Final

sports.content: George Russell secured pole for the Azerbaijan Grand Prix in Baku on Friday with a lap of 1:42.526, 0.837 seconds faster than Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc. McLaren’s Oscar Piastri qualified third, 0.001 seconds behind Leclerc. Russell is second in the championship, 81 points behind teammate and series leader Kimi Antonelli. Antonelli hit the inside barrier at Turn 1 during Q1, damaging the front-left suspension and ending his session. His earlier time was enough to place him 16th on the grid. Russell starts ahead of Leclerc and Piastri in Saturday’s race, scheduled a day early because Sunday is a national holiday in Azerbaijan.

sports.content: Team Europe took a 3-1 lead over defending champions Team World on the opening day of the Laver Cup at London’s O2 Arena on Friday, September 25. Carlos Alcaraz and Jakub Mensik closed the day with a 6-4, 6-4 doubles win over Alexander Bublik and Taylor Fritz. Casper Ruud beat Francisco Cerundolo 6-7 (4), 6-4, 10-8 to open the contest. Brandon Nakashima levelled it by defeating Mensik 6-1, 3-6, 10-7, before Rafael Jodar restored Europe’s lead with a 6-2, 6-3 victory over Bublik.
